version_semantics.platform_version: Root product release identifier; the only platform version authority.
version_semantics.module_version: Version of an independently evolving contract or module.
version_semantics.platform_min_version: Lowest Story OS platform version that may consume a module.

release_name: Product Runtime First: WORK default + explicit Codex isolation
invariants: Skill is an adapter, not a Story OS copy.
Canonical engine exists only under episodes/_system.
Evidence files never become a second stage source.
Reality constrains capture behavior, not concept scale or fictional world existence.
Environment is a physical contract, not a visual filter.
Resolved Frame Contracts are derived caches; Story, Storyboard, story-gates and Visual Profile remain authoritative.
Large anomaly scale is not a Visual Lock failure by itself; capture credibility and promised impact are judged separately.
Image workers may run concurrently, but Production Ledger mutations remain single-writer.

Legacy single-frame scheduler concurrency remains max3; Codex subscription logical Batch may run up to five isolated image workers inside one Batch, while only one such logical Batch is allowed in flight when OPENAI_API_KEY is absent.
Fast Frame Scout may request repair but never authorizes final Production PASS.
Final Candidate Snapshot is evidence, not a second creative authority.
V2.1 Delivery Adapter must consume a verified snapshot instead of rescanning mutable publish files.
Legacy episodes are never upgraded by fabricating V2.1 PASS evidence.
Post-publish facts and metrics must not mutate the frozen release manifest.
Post-publish learning is evidence for the next story, never direct creative authority.
DATA_REVIEWED uses the canonical episode-state.json stage; no second stage system exists.
Runtime Request captures user intent/execution parameters and never becomes creative authority.
Missing user plot means auto_create; Story OS must author the story instead of asking for a plot.
A rough user plot is a seed to strengthen and rewrite, not an automatic Story Lock.
Image model defaults to gpt-image-2 when the user does not specify one.
An explicitly requested image model must not be silently substituted.
Current V2.1 Visual Lock is exactly four admission images; three-image wording is legacy-only.
Runtime DAG is execution evidence only and never a second episode state machine.
Completed valid stage targets are reused on resume instead of rerunning the whole Codex supervisor.
Warm image worker pool reuses Python process/module state only; Codex conversation state remains isolated until a safe persistent transport exists.
Plus/Codex quota percentages are never guessed; automatic telemetry records only observable counters.
Continuous image scheduling removes wave barriers but preserves max3 image workers and single-writer ledger semantics.
Rolling pre-final review can trigger early repair but can never grant final frame PASS.
Provisional release material is runtime-only and can never mutate frozen release authority.
Default protagonists are ordinary young people, not occupational tools invented to solve the anomaly.
Casual work/research/expedition may explain arrival but must not turn the protagonist into an anomaly-solving professional.
First-person POV still requires a stable Character Contract.
Character Contract is a Story Build input and never a second Episode stage.
New Story runs must pass NO-ANOMALY TEST and Character Contract validation before STORYBOARD_LOCKED.
Resolved Frame Contract binds Character Contract so character drift invalidates downstream cache.
preproduction_only never invokes image generation.
image_continue must verify handoff authority hashes and must not rewrite locked Story.
shared resource library reuses references/descriptors, never prior final episode images by default.
intro templates are structural references and must be naturally rewritten.
title is one internal candidate and is not a PUBLISH_READY requirement.
V2.2 Visual Narrative Core formal production activation is based on Episode tool_version >= 2.2.0, never mere file presence.
Legacy Episode regression inputs are NON_AUTHORITY_REGRESSION_ONLY and can never become production authority by implication.
A missing or zero-frame V2.2 Visual Narrative input can never PASS verification.
Legacy Episode final or Visual Lock reviews must not inherit V2.2-only checks unless the Episode itself is formally V2.2+.
Story OS 2.2.1 defaults to Mainland China, Chinese local residents and ordinary Chinese young adults unless the Episode explicitly overrides World Identity.
Default Chinese context constrains national/cultural context, not a single ethnicity; natural Chinese regional and ethnic diversity remains valid.
Episode World Identity overrides are explicit and replace/inherit defaults deterministically.
Character Appearance Anchor is a derived cache and never replaces Character Contract, Character Visual Contract or Visual Lock pixel master.
World Identity and Character Appearance Anchor bind Resolved Frame Contract hashes for V2.2.1+ Episodes.
V2.2.0 and earlier Episodes do not inherit V2.2.1-only pixel review checks retroactively.
Provider requested canvas is generation intent; current desktop image transport does not guarantee exact RAW pixel dimensions.
Provider RAW dimensions are measured and recorded before Normalize; safe Normalize never implies provider exact-canvas compliance.
Runtime Trace is diagnostic evidence only and never becomes a second Episode Stage source.
Route Decision explains execution choice but cannot mutate the canonical episode-state.json stage by itself.
Request Intent uses deterministic rules first; free-form LLM request rewriting is not the default execution path.
Batch Image Runtime is an execution optimization and never replaces per-frame creative authority.
Formal Production requests five images per Batch by default; Visual Lock remains outside Batch Runtime.
Every Batch output keeps an independent Frame Contract SHA, Provider Receipt, Normalize result, Ledger attempt and review.
Batch transport failure is technical and may fall back to the legacy single-frame worker without consuming content repair.
Only content failures with deviation_score >= 80 AND criticality_score >= 80 may use the High×High urgent single-frame repair path.
Other content failures wait until the current Batch original generation barrier is complete before repair arbitration.
Image Provider Runtime is an execution adapter and never becomes creative authority or Episode stage authority.
OPENAI_API_KEY is read only from process environment and must never be persisted in config, Trace, Ledger or Provider Receipt.
GPT-Image-2 Image API native n may request 1..10 images in one HTTP request.
A native multi-image response count is Provider evidence; output-index to distinct Frame semantics remains a Story OS mapping convention and requires per-frame review.
OpenAI Image API custom request canvases use divisible-by-16 dimensions while preserving the locked Story OS aspect ratio, then Normalize to the exact release canvas without crop.
Codex Subscription is a fallback transport only inside explicitly selected CODEX Runtime; WORK/WEB never fall back to it when API credentials are absent or product image transport fails.
Codex subscription logical Batch is not Provider-native multi-image and must be recorded with native_multi_image=false and single_http_request=false.
A five-frame Codex logical Batch may launch up to five isolated image-generation workers concurrently without requiring OPENAI_API_KEY.
Logical Batch generation defers Fast Scout until the original Batch generation barrier is terminal.
A technical failure in one logical Batch frame must not regenerate successful sibling frames.
Codex logical Batch technical retries use adaptive concurrency 5 to 3 to 1 and never consume content repair quota.
V2.5+ Storyboard Lock requires a machine-verified Propagation Core inside the independent Story Semantic Review.
Propagation Core learns causal structure from Golden Episodes and must not require surface cloning of location, prop, trigger action or climax image.
Post-publish L3A recognition and L3B sharing are reported separately; real platform data remains evidence, never direct creative authority.
Post-publish headline metrics expose absolute count, stage delta and efficiency/rate together when the underlying data exists.
Runtime capability probes are cached per Episode and are not repeated while fresh unless explicitly invalidated.
A Rolling Review worker without verified pixel vision may not emit REPAIR_NOW; it must defer to Final Review.
Context restore consumes a SHA-bound Resume Capsule before broad repository rescans; source authority still wins on drift.
Raw candidate attempts are budgeted separately from technical retries; technical failures never consume raw candidate budget.
Performance SLO is advisory telemetry and never a Story/Release gate.
Formal image-generation entrypoints must claim Raw Candidate Budget automatically; technical failures release the claim and do not consume candidate budget.
Caption/title/description edits must not invalidate a clean Final Visual Freeze unless visual inputs changed.
A successfully normalized image candidate is committed before Fast Scout or Rolling Review; review technical failure must not release or regenerate it.
Runtime commands must use argv/stdin/UTF-8 files; shell=True, Bash heredoc and PowerShell here-string are forbidden for canonical Story OS execution.
WORK is the default Story OS runtime; local Codex availability is a capability, not an automatic routing decision.
WORK/WEB must never silently spawn local codex.exe or consume local Codex quota; CODEX requires explicit runtime selection or an explicit Codex call.
Independent Concept/Story critic provenance may be WORK_ISOLATED, WEB_ISOLATED or CODEX_ISOLATED, but must remain fresh, source-SHA-bound and honestly isolated.
If WORK/WEB lacks product image file transport, image production pauses as HOST_ACTION_REQUIRED instead of falling back to Codex Subscription.
HOST_ACTION_REQUIRED is recorded as HOST_WAIT in runtime checkpoints and is not classified as a technical failure by itself.
Product runtime host actions use deterministic request_id history; the current request file is only a pointer and historical requests are not overwritten.
Product review requests are attempt-scoped and immutable once frozen; a different source/prompt fingerprint requires a new attempt.
Legacy Visual Profile Review supports WORK_ISOLATED/WEB_ISOLATED product review and must not require local Codex by default.
Product image import releases uncommitted candidate budget on technical failure and preserves committed budget after a real normalized candidate exists.
High-volume worker/trace JSONL files are local derived runtime logs, not Git authority; formal SHA-bound review evidence remains trackable.
legacy_adapter_note: Legacy repository adapter paths may keep historical names; product/system name is Story OS.
